passages.scripture: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.

lines.text: Not many of you should become teachers.
We who teach will be judged more strictly.
You know this truth.

passages.scripture: We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.

lines.text: All people make many mistakes.
We all stumble in many ways.
If a person never makes a mistake in what he says, he is perfect.
This person has self-control over his whole body.

passages.scripture: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can guide the whole animal.

lines.text: As an analogy, a horse is a large animal.
We want the horse to obey us.
So we put a bit into the horse’s mouth.
The bit is small.
The bit helps us command the horse.
With the bit, we guide the whole body of the horse.
The large horse follows our direction because of the small bit.

passages.scripture: Consider ships as well. Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot is inclined.

lines.text: As another analogy, ships are very large.
Strong winds drive these ships.
A very small rudder steers each ship.
The pilot controls the rudder.
The ship goes wherever the pilot wants.

passages.scripture: In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things. Consider how small a spark sets a great forest ablaze.

lines.text: The tongue is a small part of the body.
Just like how a bit is small compared to a horse.
And just like how a rudder is small compared to the whole ship.
And yet, the little tongue can boast about great things.
As another analogy, small spark can set a large forest on fire.
The tongue is like that small spark.
The tongue can cause great results, even though it is small.

passages.scripture: The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.

lines.text: The tongue is a fire.
The tongue is a world of wickedness among the parts of the body.
The tongue pollutes the whole person.
The tongue sets the course of a person's life on fire.
Hell sets the tongue on fire.

passages.scripture: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man, but no man can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

lines.text: People have tamed all kinds of animals.
People have tamed birds.
People have tamed reptiles.
People have tamed creatures of the sea.
These creatures are being tamed.
But no human can tame the tongue.
The tongue is a restless evil.
The tongue is full of deadly poison.

passages.scripture: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in God’s likeness.

lines.text: The tongue is a part of the human body.
We use the tongue to speak.
The Lord is our Heavenly Father
We use the tongue to bless our Lord.
We also use the tongue to curse people.
But God made people in the likeness of God.
So we curse people who are made in God’s likeness.

passages.scripture: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be!

lines.text: A person can speak both blessing and cursing from the same mouth.
Brothers, it is not right that the same mouth should both bless and curse.
This should not happen!

passages.scripture: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?

lines.text: As an analogy, a spring gives water.
A spring cannot give both fresh water and salt water from the same opening.
A spring gives only one kind of water.
Fresh water and salt water do not come from the same spring.

passages.scripture: My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.

lines.text: As another analogy, a fig tree cannot grow olives.
And likewise, a grapevine cannot bear figs.
A salt spring cannot produce fresh water.

passages.scripture: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.

lines.text: Who is wise among you?
Who is understanding among you?
A wise person shows their wisdom by their good conduct.
An understanding person shows their understanding by their good conduct.
A wise person must act with humility.
An understanding person must act with humility.
This humility comes from true wisdom.

passages.scripture: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.

lines.text: Do you have bitter jealousy in your heart?
Then do not boast about it.
Do you have selfish ambition in your heart?
Then do not deny the truth.
Do not be proud of jealousy.
Do not boast in selfish ambition.
Do not lie against the truth because of these things.
Do not deny the truth.

passages.scripture: Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.

lines.text: This wisdom does not come from God.
The heavens are above the earth.
This wisdom does not come from heaven above.
This wisdom is earthly.
This wisdom is unspiritual.
This wisdom is demonic.

passages.scripture: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.

lines.text: Jealousy is a strong feeling of wanting what belongs to others.
Selfish ambition means seeking your own advantage above other people.
Where people have jealousy and selfish ambition, trouble follows.
Disorder will be present in that place.
Every kind of evil practice will also be found there.

passages.scripture: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.

lines.text: The wisdom from heaven above comes from God.
This wisdom is pure.
This wisdom loves peace.
This wisdom is gentle.
This wisdom is willing to yield.
This wisdom is full of mercy.
This wisdom produces good fruit.
This wisdom does not show favoritism.
This wisdom is sincere.

passages.scripture: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.

lines.text: Peacemakers act in peace.
Peacemakers plant seeds in peace.
These peacemakers harvest righteousness.
Their actions produce the fruit of righteousness.
